category: multi-hoster (free premium link generator, long-running template)

free_tier.stated: Premium-Leech is a free premium link generator: the leeched files are stored on our secure server and sent to you at maximum speed without any hourly limits or ads.
free_tier.notes: No quota, no counter, no pricing and no status page. 'Unlimited' is the vendor's adjective.

retention.stated: The leeched files are stored on our secure server - no retention period is published for that storage

egress.terms: Sent to you at maximum speed without any hourly limits or ads. No allowance is published and no throughput was measured.

interface_detail: Per-host HTML pages, one per host, each a web form. No API, no plugin, no account.
tooling: Browser only. Each host has its own static page, which is a 2010s SEO pattern rather than an API surface.
chaining: Its catalogue overlaps the current services on 76 hosts, so it adds no coverage a paid provider does not already have, and it publishes no counter that a monthly plan could be built on.

limits.value: generated links are single-user; no numeric concurrency or volume limit published
unstated; the site advertises 'no hourly limits'

limits_note: The host catalogue is the artefact: 227 host pages, of which 87 appear on none of the three current host lists compared (Debridly, World-Debrid, debridr), including rapidshare, zippyshare, uploaded, share-online, netload, fileflyer, filesflash and megashares. zippyshare.com now serves a page titled 'Zippyshare.com - [now defunct] Free File Hosting', and rapidshare.com resolves to 0.0.0.0.
binding_note: No published quota and no measurement, so no constraint can be named as the one that fails first. A 227-host catalogue in which 38% of the hosts are dead brands means the likely first failure is a host that no longer exists, not a byte counter.

identity_cost.detail: No signup: 'No signup required' in the page's own sentence.

reliability_note: A catalogue that still lists rapidshare, zippyshare, share-online and netload has not been maintained against host churn for years, so a large share of its advertised coverage returns a dead link rather than a quota error.
confidence_note: The vendor page is captured and quoted: free, no signup, no hourly limits, 220+ hosts, script status Working. No capacity figure is published so none is measured; the stale-catalogue count is a set comparison (inferred) and no unlock was attempted.

evidence.proved: 'premium download link for free (No signup required)', 'without any hourly limits or ads', and a 227-entry host list including rapidshare, zippyshare, uploaded, share-online.biz, netload.in, fileflyer and megashares
the page title is 'Zippyshare.com - [now defunct] Free File Hosting', so one catalogued host is confirmed dead

notes: PrimeLeech.com (primeleech.com) publishes the same 227-host count and the same page shape, with a different sentence set; it is recorded here rather than as a second provider because counting both would double an unmeasured capacity. The 87-of-227 stale-host figure comes from a set comparison run on 2026-10-23 against the host lists of Debridly, World-Debrid and debridr (three lists, not four). An operator that will not state a limit has not made a claim that can be relied on, and that absence is the finding.
